title: An Aged Observer
caption: The decommissioned Swedish-ESO Submillimeter Telescope reflecting the night sky, La Silla Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The large dish of the Swedish-ESO Submillimeter Telescope, or SEST, still stands at La Silla Observatory in Chile, its reflective surface acting as a mirror for the night sky.

ESO's observatories on the Chilean mountains of La Silla, Paranal and the Chajnantor Plateau host a wide range of telescopes built and run by the organization's 16 Member States. Over time, older telescopes are overtaken by newer ones, and SEST is one of these veterans.

Built at La Silla in 1987, it broke new ground as the only large telescope in the southern hemisphere studying submillimeter radio waves from objects in the distant Universe. With its 15-meter dish it could study some of the most extreme events and objects in the cosmos. In time, newer facilities on the Chajnantor Plateau, ALMA and APEX, began producing better observations, and SEST was decommissioned in 2003. It no longer observes, but its dish remains on the mountain.
